hypothesis: A Cortex would-have hold that sees a SHOCK session does better net of costs when its stop is raised on the first SHOCK session to the higher of the current stop and that session's close less one ATR(14), than under the stop rule the book follows today. One lineage per family F1 to F6. A pass is recorded only; the live rule, every gate, sizing, book and status stay as they are, and returning the rule to live needs the Owner and a later spec version.
market_rule: each market is counted and tested on its own forward holds; a lineage and its plan are per market
population: a would-have hold of the family in either arm (live or shadow) that was filled, has closed (an exit date is on file) and saw at least one SHOCK session after its fill session and before its exit session; the SHOCK state is the market's stored daily state after hysteresis; one hold is one decision (book, code, arm, decision date)
base_path: the hold as the app scores it today: the stored plan of the decision walked bar by bar with the app's fill model (limit entry, intraday stop fills at the level or at the open when the open is below it, close-signal exits at the next open)
tight_path: the same walk with one change: at the close of the first SHOCK session of the hold the stop level becomes the higher of the level in force and that session's close less 1 x ATR(14) (Wilder, on the code's raw daily bars up to and including that session); the raised level applies from the open of the next session and is filled by the same intraday stop model (at the level, or at the open when the open is below it, which is the next open after a breach); every later move of the stop is the same as in the base path; the level never goes down
outcome: net outcome of each path in parts per million of the entry fill value (net of both brokerage legs, as the app scores it, rounded half away from zero); the paired difference of a hold is the tight path less the base path
counter: the number of recorded holds of the family (one row each), counted before any difference is formed; the look needs this count to reach n
below_n: INCONCLUSIVE: no look is taken and no difference is formed; the plan stays frozen and the one look waits for the night the count reaches n
recording: a row is written when a qualifying hold closes (the two paths are computed once, from the stored decision and the bars); a hold whose recomputed base path does not reproduce the stored exit date and net is left out and counted, never written
variant_cap: the comparator counts as one stop variant of its family in the quarter of its first row, through the existing check (the family's stop and sizing variants registered this quarter plus one must not exceed the cap of three, O-46); with the cap full the step writes nothing for that family, the meter reads blocked, and it tries again on the next night, so it starts in the next quarter
statistic: the mean paired difference in parts per million
interval: one-sided 90 % lower bound: the 0.10 quantile of 2000 stationary block-bootstrap replicate means resampling the first-SHOCK sessions of the holds (holds that share a first SHOCK session are one cluster), expected block 3 sessions, seeded per lineage
pass_rule: PASS when the lower bound of the mean difference is above zero; NULL when it is not; INCONCLUSIVE and spent when the statistic cannot be computed (an undefined bootstrap)
consequence: a PASS is recorded; returning the rule to live needs the Owner and a later spec version; a NULL leaves the rule as it is; nothing here changes a stop, a gate, a size or a book
